snippet.textDisplay: I used to work with an agency that provide state program for home care. It is a program for low income, disabled and/or elderly, it is for their family to be able to take care of their loved ones at home. This program truly save millions of dollars because it prevent them from entering into nursing facilities that are more costly and quite frankly provided less care to their patients. It doesn't pay the best dollars but it help them being able to being the best caregivers without worrying if they could eat or pay bill. I really do want to see this program being expanded to middle income people. The financial qualifications is so strict that if you have little mote assets, you will no longer qualify for it.

snippet.textDisplay:
@Ambra-p3yThat’s false. If you don’t want to read that long, living longer isn’t the problem, living long while being useless is. And grandmothers aren’t useless as they contribute A LOT to a child’s likelihood of living long, healthy, happy lives.
If you want to read the full thing, then here you go.If you haven’t heard there is something called the Hispanic paradox. Where despite living in poor countries and even in diasporas like the US, Hispanics live longer than white people. Despite the socioeconomic disadvantages they have. This is mainly due to 2 factors, lifestyle and a focus on community and family in Hispanic Culture. If you look at the Family Madrigal and Coco (yes I know they are cartoony depictions but they are still accurate) you see elderly people like Mama Coco and Abuela and extended families like cousins living together all in one house. This was normal and it still is in rural Hispanic communities, where extended families live together and they live LONG. My great-great grandmother actually managed to live to over 100 years old and my grandma still remembers her. My great-grandpa lived almost to 100 and died 4 years after I was born. The real culprit is the fact that in this modern lifestyle we eat a lot of ultra-processed foods and many we sit all day. Despite my family’s longevity and great health in Mexico, my uncle whose hardly any older than 40 already has diabetes because of the lifestyle we have in America. Also, have you noticed that grandmas are ASTRONOMICALLY rare in nature? There is only a few dozen species of animals that have grandmothers. But it is even rarer to have a grandmother that takes care of children (like a dozen) and not to mention those with menopause (5). And in all of those animals (like elephants, chimps, and orcas), we find an incredible intellectual capacity, longevity, and success out in nature. Statistically, having a grandmother significantly raises your quality of life, happiness, and likelihood to be successful in all areas of life; all while significantly decreasing the likelihood of depression, suicide, and mental health problems.

This was normal and it still is in rural Hispanic communities, where extended families live together and they live LONG. My great-great grandmother actually managed to live to over 100 years old and my grandma still remembers her. My great-grandpa lived almost to 100 and died 4 years after I was born. The real culprit is the fact that in this modern lifestyle we eat a lot of ultra-processed foods and many we sit all day. Despite my family’s longevity and great health in Mexico, my uncle whose hardly any older than 40 already has diabetes because of the lifestyle we have in America. Also, have you noticed that grandmas are ASTRONOMICALLY rare in nature? There is only a few dozen species of animals that have grandmothers. But it is even rarer to have a grandmother that takes care of children (like a dozen) and not to mention those with menopause (5). And in all of those animals (like elephants, chimps, and orcas), we find an incredible intellectual capacity, longevity, and success out in nature. Statistically, having a grandmother significantly raises your quality of life, happiness, and likelihood to be successful in all areas of life; all while significantly decreasing the likelihood of depression, suicide, and mental health problems.
